Documentation → Releases → 2.8.0

SATOM 2.8.0

Rediscovery finally uses your imported CAs, rediscovery gets a Stop button, and Node TLS certificate changes show each step and warn about the web server reload.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
On this page
  • In short
  • What's new
  • Stop button for Discovery / Rediscovery
  • Content view in the TLS trust store
  • What changes for you
  • TLS trust store: one Save button per slot
  • Node TLS: certificate activation shows each step
  • A clear warning about the web server reload
  • New check after the reload
  • Fixed
  • Rediscovery ignored the TLS trust store
  • Learn more

Released: 2026-10-02 · All releases

In short#

This release is about certificates and about control over long sweeps. Rediscovery now trusts the private CAs you imported in the TLS trust store, the trust store page is easier to use, a rediscovery can be stopped, and changing the console's own certificate under Node TLS now shows what is happening and tells you clearly what to expect when the web server reloads.

What's new#

Stop button for Discovery / Rediscovery#

  • A Stop button appears while a sweep is running. Anyone allowed to start a rediscovery can stop it.
  • The sweep stops once the request it is waiting on returns, and saves no snapshot, so the previous complete snapshot is kept.
  • Stopping during the sweep also skips the deep capture and CLI capture. If one of those passes has already started, it runs to its end.
  • A stopped sweep ends in a new Stopped state that records who stopped it.
  • A sweep marked as running whose worker has already gone is closed right away. A sweep run by the other cluster node cannot be stopped from here. A leftover stop request from an earlier run is cleared when a new run starts.

Content view in the TLS trust store#

A new Content action opens the decoded certificate: subject, issuer, serial number, validity, key, signature algorithm, SHA-256 and SHA-1 fingerprints and every extension, plus the PEM text, with Copy and Download buttons.

What changes for you#

TLS trust store: one Save button per slot#

Save root CA and Save intermediate CA replace the single Import button. Each one saves only its own box (plus the name and note). The reply tells you which role every certificate was filed under, so if you paste a certificate in the wrong box you are told, instead of it being silently re-labelled.

The row and test buttons on the trust store page now look the same as the other buttons in Settings.

Node TLS: certificate activation shows each step#

Under Settings → Node TLS, importing a certificate (pasted or uploaded), issuing one from the internal CA and renewing now run as jobs. A progress panel on the tab shows each step:

  1. check (or create) the certificate;
  2. write the files;
  3. test the web server configuration;
  4. reload the web server;
  5. check that the web server now serves the new certificate.

If something fails and the previous certificate is put back, that step is shown too. Mistakes in what you entered are still reported immediately. If the node has to hand the work over to its privileged update service, the panel says so and shows how long it has waited (up to 90 seconds), instead of a frozen button.

A clear warning about the web server reload#

Changing the certificate reloads the web server that serves the console. You are now always told so: in a confirmation before you start, in a warning in the panel, and in a reminder after success. Open connections move to the new certificate. If the page stops responding or the browser shows a certificate warning, close every browser window and open SATOM again.

If the page loses contact with the node right after the switch, the panel explains that this is expected, keeps retrying for three minutes, and points you to the Jobs page, where the outcome is kept.

New check after the reload#

After the reload, SATOM connects to itself and compares the certificate it is actually serving with the one it just installed. If they differ, the job ends with a warning (nothing is rolled back, because the web server accepted the files). This check runs only when you change the certificate from the console; the nightly automatic renewal does not run it.

Fixed#

Rediscovery ignored the TLS trust store#

Even with the root and intermediate CAs saved under Settings → TLS trust store, a rediscovery could fail with certificate verify failed, while Test TLS on the same page said the device was verified. Sweeps, jobs and scheduled actions were checking devices against public CAs only. They now use your imported CAs too. If the trust store cannot be read at all, SATOM still falls back to public CAs, never to no verification.
